primitives.name: Emotional Delay Effect
primitives.verbatim_quote: One may get angrier in thinking over one's insult than at the moment of receiving it; and we melt more over a mother who is dead than we ever did when she was living.
primitives.assumptions: Emotional response is non-linear with respect to temporal delay and cognitive processing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Δt > threshold, emotional magnitude exceeds immediate stimulus value.

layer2.mapping: Time-delayed emotional feedback loop maps to stochastic differential equation with memory kernel.
layer2.telemetry: Change in emotional intensity over time post-stimulus

primitives.name: Grief Physiognomic Paralysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Lange, describes them : \ "The chief feature in the physiognomy of grief is perhaps its paralyzing effect on the voluntary movements.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F': 'muscle force in newtons', 'v': 'movement velocity in meters per second', 'η': 'motoric fatigue coefficient'}
primitives.assumptions: Voluntary movement is governed by a weakened motor control system under grief.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Motoric fatigue η → ∞ implies near-complete paralysis.

layer2.mapping: Physiological paralysis maps to reduced control authority in state-space dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Observable motoric slowness and vocal weakness

primitives.name: Object of Emotion
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the rest of the chapter I shall use the word object of emotion indifferently to mean one which is physically present or one which is merely thought of.
primitives.assumptions: Emotion objects are defined regardless of physical instantiation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P = 0, object is conceptual; when P = 1, object is sensory.

layer2.mapping: Conceptual vs. physical object space maps to dual vector spaces in emotional manifold.
layer2.telemetry: Categorization of emotional triggers as internal or external
